name: ericw-tools 0.18.1 (Quake 1)
summary: The qbsp, vis and light map compilers for Quake 1, plus bspinfo and bsputil.
description:
ericw-tools is Eric Wasylishen's continuation of Tyrann's tyrutils. This profile describes release v0.18.1, which is the newest release upstream has not marked a pre-release: the whole 2.0 line, up to 2.0.0-alpha11, is published as a pre-release and is not what a Q1 build should default to. A profile for that line is a separate document and a separate decision.

The five programs are one profile because they are one download, one licence and one version. What each of them does is measured, not assumed: qbsp writes the .bsp, and beside it the .prt that vis needs, the .pts point file when the map leaks, and its own .log. vis and light do not write a new file — they read the .bsp they were handed and save it back over itself, which is why their outputs are declared `in_place` rather than at a path this document invented. vis additionally opens the .prt of the same stem in the same directory without being told to, which is why the .prt is declared `stage_with` the .bsp: staged into its own directory, as every other input is, it would be somewhere vis never looks.

Every adjustable knob is a declared, typed option. There is no free-text argument box, so the command preview a user approves is the command that runs.

license.name: GNU General Public License v3.0 or later
license.notice: ericw-tools is somebody else's program, under its own licence, and describing it here changes nothing about that. Its own source terms are GPL-2.0-or-later; the official binaries link Embree, and its README states that builds using Embree are licensed under GPLv3+ for compatibility with the Apache licence, so GPL-3.0-or-later is what the downloadable build is conveyed under. The corresponding source for exactly this version is the v0.18.1 tag named above. Auto-Pigeon Companion is MIT and separate: it runs these programs as separate processes and does not contain, link or relicense them.

capabilities.title: Compile a Quake 1 map into a BSP
capabilities.description: Reads .map source and writes the BSP, the portal file vis needs, and a point file when the map leaks.

capabilities.title: Report what is inside a BSP
capabilities.description: bspinfo prints its report and writes no file, so this capability consumes a BSP and produces nothing: the report is the job's captured output.

capabilities.title: Check a BSP for internal inconsistencies
capabilities.description: bsputil --check prints what it found and writes no file.

actions.title: Compile the map
actions.description: qbsp reads the .map and writes the .bsp. The WAD the map names in its worldspawn is found beside the .map, which is why the optional `wad` input is staged with the source. A map that names its WAD with a folder — `gfx/metal.wad`, as every map id Software released does — is found only through `-wadpath`, so the optional texture folder is passed that way when it is set; with none set, nothing changes.

options.name: basename
options.title: Output name
options.description: The stem of the .bsp and of the files qbsp writes beside it.

options.name: leaktest
options.title: Fail if the map leaks
options.description: qbsp exits non-zero on a leak instead of writing a BSP with no visibility data. The point file is still written, and is what you load in the editor to find the hole.

options.name: bsp2
options.title: BSP2 format
options.description: For maps that exceed the limits of the original format. Needs an engine that reads BSP2.

options.name: subdivide
options.title: Texture subdivision
options.description: qbsp's default is 240. Leave it unset to use it.

diagnostics.message: The map leaks: there is a gap between the inside and the void.
diagnostics.hint: Load the .pts point file this build published in your editor and follow it to the hole.

diagnostics.message: A point file was written; it is the `pts` artifact of this build.
qbsp stopped rather than write a BSP for a map that leaks.
diagnostics.hint: Turn the leak test off if you want the BSP anyway; it will have no visibility data.

diagnostics.message: A brush produced no faces, so the compiler dropped it.
diagnostics.hint: Its plane triples enclose no volume. Check the winding of the faces the editor wrote.

diagnostics.message: The map names no WAD the compiler could open, so every face is untextured.
diagnostics.hint: Add the .wad as the pipeline's `wad` input, or fix the `wad` key in worldspawn.

diagnostics.message: A texture the map uses is not in any WAD that was opened.
diagnostics.hint: The BSP will build, with a placeholder where that texture should be.

diagnostics.hint: The `archive … not found` lines just before it name the paths it tried. Build & Run refuses a build like this.

diagnostics.message: A WAD the map names was not where the compiler looked.
diagnostics.hint: The map's `wad` key names the path; the texture bundle or your own copy has to carry the WAD at that path.

diagnostics.message: A texture the map uses is not in any WAD that was opened (ericw-tools 2.0 wording).
diagnostics.hint: The BSP will build, with a placeholder where that texture should be. `skip` and the other tool textures always report this; that is expected.

diagnostics.message: An entity has no usable brushes and was dropped.
A brush has two identical planes.
The map is over a hard limit of the original BSP format.
diagnostics.hint: Turn on the BSP2 format option, and use an engine that reads it.

Writing the BSP.

roots.purpose: read the staged map source and write the compiled BSP beside it
find the texture WADs the map names, such as gfx/metal.wad (the folder those paths start from)

actions.title: Compute visibility
actions.description: vis rewrites the BSP it is given. It also opens the .prt of the same stem in the same directory, which is why that file is an input here and is staged beside the BSP.

options.name: fast
options.title: Fast, rough visibility
options.description: A quick pass for previewing. The result is not what you ship.

options.name: level
options.title: Test level
options.description: vis's own 0-4. Ignored when the fast pass is on.

diagnostics.message: vis could not read the portal file that belongs to this BSP.
diagnostics.hint: The compile stage produces it. A leaked map has none, because qbsp stops before writing one.

diagnostics.message: vis did not compute anything.
Visibility data written.

roots.purpose: rewrite the staged BSP with its visibility data

actions.title: Compute lighting
actions.description: light rewrites the BSP it is given, and writes the coloured lightmap beside it as a .lit when that is asked for.

options.name: threads
options.title: Threads
options.description: More than one thread makes light faster and makes its output differ from run to run: measured on 0.18.1, three runs of one map at four threads produced three different lightmaps, and one thread produced the same one three times. Set it to 1 for a build whose BSP is byte-identical to the last one.

options.name: sampling
options.title: Supersampling
options.description: How many samples per lightmap texel. extra4 is the slow one you use for a final build.

options.name: lit
options.title: Write a .lit file
options.description: Coloured lighting, for engines that read it.

options.name: gate
options.title: Light cutoff
options.description: Stop tracing a light below this brightness. Higher is faster and coarser; leave it unset for light's own default.

diagnostics.message: light reported how many faces received no light.
The map has no light entities in use, so the result will be fullbright or black.
light is writing a file.
light stopped before it finished.

roots.purpose: rewrite the staged BSP with its lighting data

actions.title: Report what is inside the BSP
actions.description: bspinfo prints its report; there is no file to collect, and the job's captured output is the report.
